items.title: One year after 10/10 flash crash, bitcoin and ether liquidity have rebuilt, but altcoins still face risks
items.description: Bitcoin and ether order books are deeper than before the crash, while altcoin liquidity keeps eroding and spot trading remains well below its October 2025 peak.

items.title: Tokenized commodities look beyond gold as lending and oil open new markets
items.description: Paxos Labs, Theo and Energy Substantiation execs see growth coming from putting physical assets to work, with precious metals leading and energy presenting a tougher test.

items.title: Bitcoin's $19 billion wake-up call: One-year after flash crash, has crypto learned anything?
items.description: The Oct. 10, 2025 flash crash wiped out billions in leveraged crypto bets. Traders now have better tools to spot risks, but the forces behind the selloff remain.

items.title: Bitcoin's volatility has plunged, but extreme price swings are more frequent than in 2018
items.description: CoinDesk analysis finds 10 unusually large trading days in 2026, raising questions about how investors measure risk in an increasingly institutional crypto market.

items.title: Robinhood Chain slowdown spreads from fees to trading as transactions fall more than 40%
items.description: Daily activity has dropped from 10.8 million transactions to 6.2 million since mid-September even as Robinhood keeps paying network fees on customer swaps.

items.title: XRP Ledger patched decade-old bug that could create billions of dollars in XRP from nothing
items.description: Researchers demonstrated how a payment could create spendable XRP without the sender funding it, prompting an emergency software release.

items.title: Visa survey says nearly half of APAC consumers open to using stablecoins by 2031
items.description: Visa’s survey of 14,250 people found interest in stablecoin payments is growing, though only 6% of respondents correctly understood how they work.

items.title: U.S. CFTC moves to fold event contracts into swaps regulations as legal fight rages
items.description: The derivatives regulator is proposing a formal rule to include certain contracts traded on platforms like Kalshi's as swaps that require the agency's oversight.

items.title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
items.description: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

items.title: Justin Sun says Tron’s post-quantum cryptography has gone live on testnet
items.description: “We’re ready to bring quantum resistance to mainnet at any time,” Sun said in a post on X.

items.title: Tech chief says EU can fend off rogue AI risk: Report
items.description: There are global concerns following incidents at OpenAI ‌and Anthropic, and fears have arisen that rogue AI agents may venture beyond human control.

items.title: Sam Altman-backed Bitcoin life insurer, Meanwhile, raises more funds
items.description: The round follows increased international demand for Meanwhile’s Bitcoin life insurance policies amid broader macro instability.

items.title: US plans to seize $1B in crypto linked to Iran this week: Scott Bessent
items.description: The Treasury Department has announced several digital asset seizures related to sanctions on Iran as part of US sanctions.

items.title: New York permanently bars Celsius founder Mashinsky in $35M fraud settlement
items.description: The agreement resolves a 2023 civil fraud lawsuit against the Celsius founder and permanently bars him from the cryptocurrency, securities and commodities industries.

items.title: THORChain exec accuses Tether of temporarily freezing USDT vaults
items.description: Chad Barraford, technical co-founder of the network, said that the funds were frozen and then unfrozen without explanation.

items.title: HSBC, Ant Digital test AI-agent payments using tokenized deposits
items.description: The technical trial showed how AI agents could discover services and make micropayments using HSBC’s tokenized deposits, with real-time settlement and risk checks.

items.title: Vance says Microsoft replaced laid-off workers with foreign hires. Here’s what the visa data shows
items.description: The administration barred Microsoft and seven other firms from sponsoring green cards over claims they favor foreign workers. Here's what the visa data shows.

items.title: Microsoft's Nadella says AI needs an ‘emergency brake’ that humans control
items.description: Nadella joined other tech moguls and researchers in calling for stronger safeguards and, in some cases, for the pacing of frontier development.

items.title: Nvidia GPUs are everywhere. Here are the ways companies are accessing them
items.description: One industry researcher identified over 300 neoclouds that can provide GPU capacity, up about 55% in less than a year.

items.title: Putin relayed Iran war proposal to Trump, Kremlin says

items.title: Trump's diesel agreement with Putin accused of contradicting Russia sanctions law
items.description: Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a searing statement that the U.S. easing sanctions on Moscow "plays into Russia's hands."

items.title: How Supreme Court justices are leaning in major 401(k) case over private funds and underperformance
